blocks.text: You can add users to Authentication Service by creating them locally within Authentication Service or via an external identity provider (IdP) provider. In addition, you can assign them admin entitlements to make them administrators for a Zscaler service (e.g., Internet & SaaS (ZIA), Private Access (ZPA)) or you can assign them service entitlements so they are able to authenticate to a Zscaler service as an end user.

If your organization uses Unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), administrator roles for Authentication Service and some Zscaler services are managed on a different Role Management page. To learn more, see About Role Management. Unified RBAC is a feature in limited availability. To access Unified RBAC, contact your Zscaler Account team.
Managing users provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Control which users within your organization are service admins or assigned to a Zscaler service.
Assign users to a single or multiple Zscaler services.
Assign users with administrator roles to manage specific Zscaler services.
Manage all users in Authentication Service instead of maintaining individual user databases in each of the subscribed Zscaler services.

blocks.text: On the Users page (Administration > Authentication > Users), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Click the Filter icon to display the search options. You can search for a user by username or group name.
Reset the page to the default view.
Import new users, or modify existing users, using a CSV file.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Reset the password for multiple users. This option is visible only when you select more than one user.
Perform a bulk action on the users, like activate, deactivate, or delete them. This option is visible only when you select more than one user.
View a list of configured users. For each user, you can see:
Name: The user's display name, which is visible throughout the Zscaler Admin Console.
Login ID: The user's login ID.
Groups: The number of groups that a user is assigned to.
Status: The status of the user (Active or Inactive).
Select users to perform bulk operations on them. You must select more than one user to view the bulk actions.
Edit or delete the user details.
Click the icon and activate or deactivate the user.
